Hotel stocks fall on the West Asia conflict
Warburg completes the APG stake purchase in Fleur
stockEventsSrc: NSE closes (weekly series in the model); company filings; ICICI Direct and PL (52-week range, Aug-2026)
moat: Brand and cost leadership in India's mid-market: the largest mid-priced chain, owned hotels at 76% occupancy, hotel-level EBITDAR margins of ~50-60% on owned assets, 2.5 m loyalty members and 45% repeat demand that fill newly managed hotels quickly. Not a pricing moat: ARR (Rs6,361 in Q1FY27) is set by local supply, and mid-market brands are easier to copy than luxury ones.
critiques: ARR growth has stalled: +2% in Q1FY27 and flat in Q2FY26; occupancy gains were bought through retail channels (commissions) when corporate travel weakened.

Margins have fallen for two years (FY25 49.3%, FY26 47.8%, Q1FY27 43.4%) on renovation, technology and the GST change; the 50% FY28 margin is a management promise that depends on renovation spend ending and rates rising above Rs7,500.
A fifth of the profit belongs to someone else: Warburg Pincus owns 41.09% of Fleur, which holds most of the owned hotels; minorities took 21% of FY26 profit after tax.

The scheme is complex and still needs SEBI, exchange, NCLT, shareholder and creditor approval; completion in CY2027 is management's estimate and has already slipped (CRISIL: 9-12 months from Jul-2026).

Fleur plans to deploy ~Rs2,500-3,000 cr (Warburg's Rs960 cr plus debt) on acquisitions and developments; returns on that capital (current Fleur ROCE ~12.5-13%) are uncertain, and Lemon Tree shareholders bear 74% of it after the scheme.
Debt is still heavy for a hotel company: Rs1,500 cr of bank debt plus Rs503 cr of leases at Mar-26 (2.15x net EBITDA), while IHCL, EIH and ITC Hotels are net cash.
Promoter holding is only ~22%; the founder is moving to a non-executive role at Lemon Tree from Mar-2027 and will focus on Fleur.
gaps: ICICI Securities' (Rs151), IDBI Capital's (Rs165) and Keynote's (Rs124) valuation methods and estimates are not public; Motilal Oswal's note was seen only through a DSIJ summary (17x / 30x EV/EBITDA, FY28).
Named shareholders at Jun-2026: the BSE shareholding page refused our tool (HTTP 403), so named holders are from AR FY26 (31-Mar-2026); categories are Jun-2026 (Screener, PL).

Fleur Hotels' own consolidated net debt is not disclosed; the minority deduction uses the minorities' share of profit (21.2% in FY26) applied to consolidated equity value instead of a Fleur-level split.
Warburg Pincus's price for APG's 41.09% of Fleur was not disclosed; the timing and price of its Rs960 cr primary infusion are not known.
Capex for Aurika Nehru Place (572 rooms) is 'to be announced'; not in our forecasts.
A Macquarie Outperform with a Rs180 target appears in a search summary without a date we can verify; left out.
conflicts: EBITDA definition: company 'net EBITDA' FY26 Rs699.3 cr includes other income (Rs8.2 cr); Screener and our model use operating EBITDA Rs690 cr. Q1FY27 Rs151.9 cr vs Rs149 cr.

Debt: company 'total debt' Rs1,500 cr (Mar-26) excludes Rs503 cr of lease liabilities that Screener includes in borrowings (Rs2,004 cr); management also quotes Rs1,275 cr net of cash (Jun-26). We use Screener's figure incl. leases, with EBITDA post-Ind AS 116.
Scheme timing: CFO hoped for H1 CY2027; the Executive Chairman said 'conservatively ... the late second half of next year' (10-Aug-2026 call); the Jan-2026 deck said 12-15 months.
CRISIL quotes FY25 interest cover as 3.83x in its text and 3.06x in its table.
